"The Black Hand" is a silent short film released in 1906, directed by Wallace McCutcheon Sr. It is considered one of the earliest crime films and is based on the real-life criminal organization known as the Black Hand, which was active in the early 20th century in the United States. The film follows a plot in which a group of criminals known as the Black Hand engage in extortion and kidnapping.

The film is notable for its early use of intertitles to convey dialogue and advance the plot, as well as its use of dramatic lighting and shadow effects to create tension and suspense. The Black Hand was a popular subject in early cinema, as the criminal organization was widely feared and sensationalized in the media at the time.

Overall, "The Black Hand" is an important early example of crime cinema and demonstrates the evolving techniques and storytelling conventions of the silent film era.
